changes.quote: Maximum Front End Advance | Tier 0 800+ | New (up to 72 Month Terms) up to 125%
changes.note: Two whole tables the record did not have. The front-end advance matrix is 4 rows x 5 tiers = 20 cells, transcribed in full: only Tier 0 on a new unit at 72 months or less gets 125%, and everything at Tier 2 and below is 110%. The record showed only the 140% total advance, which is a different number and does not tell the desk what it can put on the front. The term grid is 14 rows: PNC caps term by model year AND vehicle value, so a 2019 unit is 66 months and anything valued $5K-$10K is 60 regardless of year.

ambiguities.note: Record says "N/A (flat fee model)". This sheet states no chargeback policy either way — same unsourced inference as chase. The BuyDown section does describe an ACH debit when the net buy-down is negative, which is not the same thing.
Record says "Not specified in documents". Confirmed — this sheet says nothing about income documentation.
